div.head: II Cn 27
div.ab: And se ðe on gemote mid wiðertihtlan hine sylfne oððon his mann werige, hæbbe þæt eall forspecen, ⁊ geandwerde ðam oþrum, swa hundrede riht þynce.
And se ðe on gemote mid wiðertihtlan hine sylfne oððe his man werige, habbe þæt eal forspecen, ⁊ geandwyrde þam oðran, swa hundred riht þince.
Et qui in placito se ipsum uel hominem suum distortis compellationibus defendere presumpserit, habeat totum hoc forspecen (cassatum), et contingat de reliquo, sicut hundreto rectum uidebitur.
⁊ se on gemote mid wiðertihtlan hine sylfne oððe his man werie, hæbbe eall þæt forspecen ⁊ geandwyrde ðam oðrum, swa hundrede riht ðynce.

And he who in Court tries to protect either himself or one of his men by bringing a countercharge shall have wasted his words, and shall meet the charge brought by his opponent in such a way as the hundred court shall determine.
And he who defends himself or his man in court by a counter-charge shall have spoken this all in vain, and is to answer the other as seems right to the hundred.
Und wer im Gericht sich selbst oder seinen Untergebenen vertheidigt durch Widerklage[n?], habe dies alles vergeblich gesprochen, und antworte dem Gegner, wie dem Hundertgericht richtig dünkt.
And whoever in court defends himself or his man by counter-accusation(s?), let all of it count as said in vain, and let him answer his opponent as seems right to the hundred.
